correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed F(x)=J(sigma(x),x) with sign sigma(u)=+1 and sigma(u_n)=-1 for distinct u_n->u in S_X. Because ||(sigma(x),x)||_infty=1, F maps S_X into itself. Isometry of J gives exact distance max(|sigma(x)-sigma(y)|,||x-y||), so F never contracts and is injective. Yet ||F(u)-F(u_n)||=2 while ||u-u_n||->0; every 0<epsilon<2 is expanded by >epsilon with no contraction depth. For c and ell_infty, coordinate prepending is a surjective linear max-sum isometry; no continuity is required of a noncontractive map. Infinite-dimensionality ensures u_n exists.
residual_risks: Only real Banach X satisfying an isometric max-sum self-embedding; no assertion for ell_1 or spaces without that embedding.

evidence: Levchenko–Zavarzina establish plain sphere plasticity for c and ell_infinity, and strong plasticity for Hilbert spheres.
General uniform strong-plasticity results of Kadets–Zavarzina/Naimpally et al. concern totally bounded spaces and therefore do not apply to these infinite-dimensional spheres.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Ordinary plasticity for bijections does not prevent injective non-surjective expanding self-maps. A theorem for totally bounded domains cannot subsume these Banach spheres.
